purpose: Test whether the react-* knowledge prose (12 skills, ~2,497 lines) changes answer quality beyond what the base model produces. These are quality/routing cases, not effect-boundary cases, so they are kept separate from high_use_cases.json and are not parsed by validate_registry.py.

arms.A_control: Active registry WITH the react-* family installed (routes via react-expert or a focused react-* skill).
arms.B_bare: Active registry WITH react-* removed. Base model only, no react guidance.
arms.C_substitute: react-* removed, plus the proposed replacement context: eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules + React Testing Library conventions (see docs/react-substitute-note.md).

protocol: Run each case 3x per arm in fresh context. Score each answer 0-1: (fraction of must_include anchors satisfied) minus 0.34 for each must_avoid anchor present, floored at 0. Record raw answers before scores in a dated results/ file. A rubric-judge model may score, but must see the anchors, not the arm label.
gate: The family is safe to EVICT when mean(B) >= mean(A) - 0.10 AND arm B commits no must_avoid violation on any case where arm A commits none. A case where A beats B by >0.25 and C does NOT recover it flags that specific sub-skill as a CONVERT candidate (keep a check, not the prose), not a blanket keep.

cases.prompt: This component keeps `fullName` in state and updates it with a useEffect that runs whenever firstName or lastName change. Is this the right approach?
must_include: derive fullName during render instead of storing it
remove the redundant state and the effect
effects are for synchronizing with external systems, not computing values
must_avoid: only suggesting to fix the dependency array

cases.prompt: I have a useEffect with an empty dependency array that starts a setInterval calling setCount(count + 1), but count is stuck at 1. Why, and how do I fix it?
must_include: the interval closes over the initial count (stale closure)
use the functional updater setCount(c => c + 1)
explain why empty deps captures count once
must_avoid: adding count to the dependency array without noting it tears down and recreates the interval every tick
recommending a third-party library as the primary fix

cases.prompt: I subscribe to a WebSocket inside a useEffect and call setMessages when data arrives. There is no return value from the effect. Anything wrong?
must_include: return a cleanup function that unsubscribes/closes the socket
otherwise subscriptions leak and stack across renders/unmounts
StrictMode double-invokes effects in dev so cleanup must be correct

cases.prompt: My list renders items with key={index}. When I delete or reorder rows, the wrong row's input state moves around. What's going on?
must_include: index keys tie React state to position, not identity
use a stable unique id from the data as the key
explain reconciliation reusing the wrong element state
must_avoid: suggesting a fresh random key each render

cases.prompt: To make our app fast, I wrapped every component in React.memo and every prop value in useMemo/useCallback. Good practice?
must_include: push back: blanket memoization adds cost and complexity for usually-negligible benefit
measure first (profiler) and memoize proven hot paths
the legitimate cases are referential stability for deps and genuinely expensive renders

cases.prompt: I fetch in a useEffect keyed on a prop id and setState with the result. When the id changes quickly I sometimes see the wrong data flash. How should I structure this?
must_include: it's a race: a slow earlier response resolves after a newer one
cancel or ignore stale responses (AbortController or an ignore flag in cleanup)
consider a query library or router loader that handles this

cases.prompt: One React context holds a big object with many fields. Any field change re-renders the whole tree. What are my options?
must_include: split into multiple narrower contexts by change frequency
memoize the provided value
or use a selector-based store (e.g. useSyncExternalStore / a state library)
must_avoid: saying context is always the wrong tool

cases.prompt: My form re-renders on every keystroke and I want per-field validation and dirty tracking without janky typing. How should I build it?
must_include: weigh controlled vs uncontrolled inputs (uncontrolled/refs avoid per-keystroke re-render)
isolate field state so one field's change doesn't re-render the whole form
define validation timing (on blur/submit vs on change)
must_avoid: only saying add an onChange handler

cases.prompt: I built a custom modal with a div overlay. Keyboard users can tab to the page behind it, focus doesn't return to the trigger on close, and Escape does nothing. How do I fix it?
must_include: trap focus within the dialog while open
restore focus to the trigger on close
role=dialog + aria-modal and an Escape handler
prefer the native <dialog> element or a maintained accessible primitive

cases.prompt: Our React tests assert on component state and instance methods, and they break every time we refactor even though the UI still works. How should we test instead?
must_include: test observable behavior, not internals
query by role/text and interact as a user (Testing Library)
this decouples tests from refactors
